frontierDelta: Reject serial Agent-controlled marginal-evidence stopping for small six-window Game trajectory packets. Preserve full one-shot as the strong baseline and make adaptive-selection overhead an explicit tractability variable before attempting another stopping mechanism.
predictionError: The bet predicted mean unique-window consumption below 0.75 and progressive decision agreement at least as good as matched random. Actual unique-window fraction was 1.00 in all 8 cases; no autonomous early stop occurred; progressive agreed with unanimous full references 6/8 while matched full one-shot agreed 8/8. The predeclared false-early-stop prediction is untested rather than satisfied because there were zero early stops.
worldModelUpdate: Research stopping competence is not obtained by repeatedly prompting an Agent to decide whether another observation matters. On small finite evidence universes, adaptive evidence-selection overhead and path-dependent deliberation can dominate evidence cost and can destabilize the final semantic conclusion even after all evidence is present.
operatorPriorUpdate: Add a conditional prior: compare adaptive-selection overhead against full-inspection cost before admitting an evidence-selection loop. For small bounded evidence sets, one-shot full inspection may be the tractable operator. Retain the broader marginal-value/stopping problem as unresolved for evidence spaces where full inspection is materially expensive.
